introHeading: The enclosed photo booth in Jersey City
introParas: Jersey City's waterfront venues sell themselves on the view — the Hudson, the Manhattan skyline lit up across the water, floor-to-ceiling windows in the Exchange Place and Paulus Hook event spaces built specifically to frame it. The enclosed booth is the deliberate counterpoint to that. Guests step inside, the curtain closes, and for a few seconds the skyline and the room disappear entirely. What comes out is a strip that has nothing to do with the view and everything to do with who was standing in front of the camera.

The cabinet's small footprint makes it an easy add at a waterfront reception where floor space near the windows is already spoken for by cocktail tables, and it works just as well in a converted loft around Journal Square or The Heights, where older buildings sometimes mean a narrower doorway or a walk-up than a newer highrise would. A 10ft x 10ft spot is ideal, 8ft x 8ft works when the room runs tighter, and it only needs a standard outlet nearby. Guests arriving from Manhattan on the PATH appreciate a fast, familiar format that doesn't require an explanation before the line starts moving.

It's a strong fit for Jersey City weddings, showers and corporate events at Newport and Grove Street venues, and for a company event the cabinet exterior wraps in your branding. There is no travel fee for most Jersey City venues — it's a short hop from our Brooklyn base — and your strip template is designed for your event, not pulled from a template menu, before we ever arrive.

faqHeading: Enclosed Booth in Jersey City — FAQ

faqs.q: Does the enclosed booth work well at a Jersey City waterfront venue?
faqs.a: It's a natural pairing. Waterfront spaces around Exchange Place and Paulus Hook are built around the view, and most of the photos taken near the windows are posed with that skyline in mind. The enclosed booth gives guests a private, unposed alternative a few steps away — a strip that's about them, not the backdrop.

faqs.q: Do you travel to Jersey City from Brooklyn, and is there a fee?
faqs.a: Yes, and there's no travel fee for most Jersey City venues since it's a short hop from our Brooklyn base. We still confirm the exact number from your venue ZIP code before you book, so there's nothing new on the invoice.

faqs.q: Can the enclosed booth fit in an older building around Journal Square or The Heights?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. The cabinet's footprint is compact and it doesn't need to be assembled inside the room if a doorway or stairwell is narrower than a newer highrise elevator. Tell us your building and floor and we'll confirm the path before your date.

faqs.q: How many people fit inside the enclosed booth?
faqs.a: Couples and small groups fit comfortably. For a bigger wedding party shot or a large group photo, we usually pair the enclosed booth with one of our open-air booths so both kinds of photo happen at the same event.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: A 10ft x 10ft spot is comfortable, and we can compress to 8ft x 8ft when a Jersey City venue's floor plan runs tight. We need a standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet of where the booth is set up.

About 20 minutes once we're on site, and we arrive a full hour ahead of your scheduled start so everything is tested and quiet before guests arrive. If your venue needs us there earlier, idle time runs at $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Can the enclosed booth be branded for a corporate event in Jersey City?
faqs.a: Yes. The exterior of the cabinet wraps in your branding and the strip template can carry your logo, which is common for the corporate events and product launches we run in the Newport and Exchange Place office towers.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Jersey City venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million liability insurance policy. If your venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact details and we'll send it over.
